summary: Ludwig Ross was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kiel University (~1825–1832). He held posts at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859), teaching Carl Siegfried.

Ludwig Sütterlin was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1882–1883) and earned his Ph.D. under Hermann Osthoff at Heidelberg University (~1883–1887). He held posts at Heidelberg (1890, 1896–1913) and chaired comparative linguistics at Freiburg (1913–1924).

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at TU Berlin, Owens College/Manchester, and Cambridge, earning his Ph.D. there in ~1929. He served as a lecturer and fellow at Trinity College (1929–1947) and philosophy professor at Cambridge (1930–1947).

Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lviv, the EPHE, and Collège de France under Stefan Stasiak, Louis Renou, Jean Przyluski, Jules Bloch, Stanisław Schayer, and Helena Willman-Grabowska. He was a professor at Breslau (1945–1978).

Ludwik Sternbach was an Indologist who studied at Jagiellonian University and Lviv under Stefan Stasiak and Helena Willman-Grabowska. He held posts at Jagiellonian (1933–1938), Lviv (1939–1941), Mumbai (1944), Sorbonne Nouvelle (1970–1972), and Collège de France (1972–1976).

Luigi Heilmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Luigi Suali and Ambrogio Ballini at Padua and Bologna. He served at Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, Pavia, Cagliari, and as professor of linguistics at Bologna (~1957–1986).
Luigi Pio Tessitori was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Paolo Emilio Pavolini at the University of Florence from ~1905 to 1910.

Luigi Suali was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Bologna under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held a post at Bologna (1907) and served as a professor at Pavia (1909–1910, 1914–1956).

Luigia Nitti-Dolci was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Paris (~1928–1938) under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Theodor Bloch. She served as editor of Nepalese manuscripts at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne (~1935–1939).

Luis Oscar Gómez was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Puerto Rico, Yale under Stanley Insler, and Michigan. He served as department chair and professor at the University of Michigan and directed Mangalam Research Center.

Luise Hercus was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. She held academic posts at St Anne's (1948–1954), the University of Adelaide (1965–1969), and the Australian National University (~1969–1991).
Luise Hilgenberg was an Indology scholar who earned a Dr.med. (-1922) and a Dr. phil. (~1927–1933) under the supervision of Willibald Kirfel at the University of Bonn.

Lumír Jisl worked in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Charles University (1940–1949), where he later served as Privatdozent (1960), and was secretary at the Institute of Archaeology of the CAS, Prague (1956).
Lungten Dubgyur is a Tibetology and law scholar who earned degrees from Sherubtse College, Government Law College in Mumbai (LL.B), and the University of Edinburgh (LL.M).

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a Tibetology and religious studies scholar who studied under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso and earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot starting in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Lutz Bieg is a sinologist who completed his doctorate at Heidelberg University (-1971) and his habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin (-1986). He served as a professor of Chinese literature and philosophy at the University of Cologne (1989–2008).
Lyne Bansat-Boudon is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied under Armand Minard and Marie-Claude Porcher, and has taught Judit Törzsök and Isabelle Ratié.

Lynette Monteiro is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa (1986–1996). She held posts at Sea Glass Psychological Services (1997) and the Ottawa Mindfulness Clinic (2003).

Lynn Struve is a sinology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Washington (~1963–1967) and the University of Michigan (~1967–1976). She held an academic post at Indiana University Bloomington (~1977).
